clue.text: Irish resort that's left with considerable speed!

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
a rush is a burst of great haste

explanation.surface: A holiday town in Ireland that everyone departs from in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTRUSH is a seaside town on the north coast of Northern Ireland. 'Left' looks like a past tense but is the nautical side.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a well-known seaside holiday destination in County Antrim.

clue.text: A man with taking ways in the main

definitions.text: A man with taking ways in the main

parts.words: A man with taking ways in the main
parts.note: taking ways sounds like charm but means stealing; the main is the open sea, not mostly

explanation.surface: A charming fellow, on the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' seems to mean 'mostly' but is the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea robber seizes ships and cargo on the ocean.

clue.text: Consider getting into horticulture — gardening

indicators.note: getting into means the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Thinking about taking up gardening as a hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard a matter is to think about it.

clue.text: Goes on or stays attached to bed?

definitions.meaning: travels on, as on a horse or bus
a ship lies at anchor, held fast to the seabed

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps going or remains in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling on something, and a ship lying at anchor fastened to the sea floor.

clue.text: Toffs maybe carrying work for a break in the journey

indicators.note: carrying means the shuffled letters hold another piece inside
maybe signals the letters of toffs might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Upper-class people with jobs stopping for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' shuffles the upper-class word into STOFF, and 'carrying' then holds the work inside it; the surface pictures toffs with jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop-off is a short halt on a trip.

clue.text: Insufferable party returning credit notes

indicators.note: returning means the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is an informal party
IOUs are written promises to pay, notes acknowledging credit

explanation.surface: An unbearable celebration sends back slips of paper acknowledging debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reads the party word backwards as OD; 'notes' makes the debt slips plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something so unpleasant it cannot be tolerated.

clue.text: Doesn't take into consideration any special reductions

definitions.meaning: price cuts offered by a shop

explanation.surface: Ignores any bargain offers.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss as unimportant, and price cuts in a sale.

clue.text: Footwear in which more than a quarter do gardening

parts.note: over means more than
S is south, a quarter of the compass
to hoe is a gardening job

explanation.surface: Boots in which a large share of the weeding is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' looks like a fraction but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber galosh worn over a shoe for protection.

clue.text: Heartless woman arranging appointments and administering tranquillisers

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is taken away

parts.note: she refers to a woman
dating is arranging romantic meetings

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted woman fixes appointments and drugs people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the H from SHE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving calming drugs is calming a patient with sedatives.

clue.text: Dance dress with bustle attached

parts.note: a rig is an outfit, a style of dress
ado is fuss and bustle
on can mean fixed or attached, as a lid that is on

explanation.surface: A dancer's gown with a padded bustle sewn on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' and 'bustle' pose as clothing; bustle here means fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The rigadoon is a lively old Provençal dance for couples.

clue.text: Using a little science, finish constructing scale

indicators.note: a little of the word science means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: to finish is to come to an end

explanation.surface: A scientist uses a bit of theory to complete building a model to scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' reads as a noun but is the verb, to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a cliff is to climb up it, to go higher.

clue.text: Stand for a beast

explanation.surface: Putting up with an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something, and the large furry mammal.

clue.text: Goes by the timbre to identify the bird

parts.note: goes, as in takes one's go, are turns
the tone of an instrument is its timbre

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher recognises a species by the quality of its song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wading shorebird that flips over pebbles to find food.

clue.text: Start shaping stone

indicators.note: shaping suggests the letters of stone are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A sculptor begins carving a block.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning.

clue.text: Idle pupil — stupid creature!

parts.note: L is a learner, as on the L-plates of a pupil driver
an oaf is a clumsy, dim person

explanation.surface: A teacher insults a lazy schoolchild as a dimwit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' reads as an adjective for the pupil but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle and to laze both mean to pass time doing nothing.

clue.text: Away on business, look over an ancient city that's run down

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the next
in a down clue, over places one piece above another

parts.note: off means away
Co is short for company, a business
lo is an old word meaning look
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Travelling for work, inspecting a ruined ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run down' looks like the city's decay but means feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off colour means feeling slightly ill or below par.

clue.text: Quickly go to seed on Merseyside

parts.note: to run is to go quickly
corn is the seed of cereal plants

explanation.surface: Plants bolting and setting seed on Merseyside.
explanation.walkthrough: RUNCORN is an industrial town on the River Mersey in north-west England; 'go to seed' looks like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The town stands on the south bank of the Mersey estuary.

clue.text: Sportsmen may be the least affected

indicators.note: affected means the letters are altered in arrangement

explanation.surface: Sporting types might be the least pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field competitors.

clue.text: Found smooth but quite rigid

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
to iron is to smooth

explanation.surface: Discovered something smooth yet stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find but is the verb to cast metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast-iron means unbending and firm, as a cast-iron guarantee.

clue.text: Jerk nabbing a blackguard for dealing

indicators.note: nabbing means one word grabs and holds the other inside it

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
raff is an old word for a worthless fellow, as in riff-raff

explanation.surface: A fool catches a scoundrel at his illicit trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nabbing' wraps the jerk around the scoundrel; raff is a rare word, best known from riff-raff.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafficking is illegal trading, as in drug dealing.

clue.text: A large number refuse to make money

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
ash is the waste left after burning

explanation.surface: Turning down a big sum in order to earn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins and notes, ready money.

clue.text: A beautiful flower spray

definitions.meaning: the classic garden bloom of romance
the perforated nozzle of a watering can, which sprinkles water

explanation.surface: A lovely bloom sprinkled with water.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden bloom, and the sprinkler head fitted to a watering can or shower.

clue.text: Reunite scattered followers

indicators.note: scattered means the letters are dispersed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Bringing together a dispersed band of supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the entourage of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: Old queen is got up in brown

indicators.note: in a down clue, got up means the run of letters reads upwards

parts.note: Queen Anne ruled Britain in the early 1700s

explanation.surface: A former queen is dressed in brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' works because this is a down clue: the queen's name and 'is' are read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy yellowish or reddish brown pigment.

clue.text: Plan a camping holiday?

definitions.meaning: playfully, staying under canvas is being inside a tent

explanation.surface: Thinking of going camping.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or purpose, and whimsically being under canvas.

clue.text: Non-drinker absorbed in one game or another

indicators.note: absorbed in means one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: loo is an old card game, one game among many
TT means teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A teetotaller engrossed in one game after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: one card game holds the teetotaller, and the result is 'another' game. 'absorbed in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbers game of chance is another game, related to bingo.

clue.text: Dressing in a suit to find a job

indicators.note: dressing means the letters are arranged, as troops are dressed into line

explanation.surface: Wearing a formal suit to get work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' rearranges the nine letters of IN A SUIT TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a post or position of employment.

clue.text: Art is strangely moving

indicators.note: strangely means the letters are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A remark that art is oddly affecting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like emotionally stirring but means in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion.

clue.text: Casual shirt — a faux pas causing great consternation

parts.note: T stands for a T-shirt
a faux pas is a social error

explanation.surface: Wearing a T-shirt to a formal event is a gaffe that causes horror.
explanation.definitionFit: Both express overwhelming fear and alarm.

clue.text: Split cane isn't used in this case

indicators.note: split means the letters are broken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A split cane is not used here.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance and a case are both examples of something.

clue.text: Guard provided by the nurse with experience

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, an old British nursing grade
to try something is to experience it

explanation.surface: Protection supplied by a seasoned nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch.

clue.text: Soldiers can't accept their comrades being craven

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers

indicators.note: accept means the word for can't takes another inside it

parts.note: the apostrophe drops to give cant
the soldiers' comrades are more Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Troops who will not take in their fellows are cowards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accept' tucks the comrades inside the contraction, giving CREANT; the soldiers' comrades are more Royal Engineers, hence the repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreant is an archaic word for cowardly.
